article.title: Accept USDC Payments in Node.js Without Stripe: A Practical 402 Walkthrough
article.body_markdown:
If you sell access to a small API, the usual answer is Stripe. But for a $5–$20 product, Stripe onboarding (KYC, payout delays, per-transaction fees, country availability) can cost more than it earns. There is an older idea that fits machine-to-machine payments better: **HTTP 402 Payment Required**.

This post shows how to charge per API call in USDC with two lines of Express middleware.

## The 402 flow in 30 seconds

1. Client calls your endpoint without paying.
2. Your server answers `402` with a JSON payment request: asset, amount, chain, recipient address.
3. Client sends the USDC transfer on-chain and retries with a tx hash.
4. Your server verifies the transfer (recipient, amount, block range) and returns the payload plus a short-lived HMAC receipt.

No API keys, no accounts, no custodian. The address is yours; funds never touch the middleware.

## Server: two lines

```js
import express from "express";
import { paymentMiddleware } from "@josealbertomaquina/usdc-paywall";

const app = express();
app.get("/v1/heavy",
  paymentMiddleware({ usdc: 0.5, chain: "base", payTo: process.env.PAY_TO }),
  (req, res) => res.json({ result: "your expensive compute here" }));
app.listen(3000);
```

The first free call gets `402` + a machine-readable payment request, so scripts and agents can pay programmatically — that's the whole point. Human clients get a 5-line curl flow documented in the README.

## Client: pay and retry

```bash
curl -i https://api.example.com/v1/heavy      # -> 402 + payment request
# send 0.5 USDC on Base to PAY_TO (any wallet), then:
curl "https://api.example.com/v1/heavy?tx=0x..."
```

Verification reads `eth_getLogs` for USDC transfers to your address in a replay window, checks amount and recipient, and issues an HMAC receipt so the next minutes don't need another on-chain roundtrip.

## When this beats Stripe (and when it doesn't)

**Beats:** per-call pricing for APIs, machine/agent clients, global availability without country onboarding, sub-cent fees on Base.

**Doesn't:** subscriptions with dunning, card-user consumers who never held crypto, jurisdictions where you must invoice in fiat. Use both: Stripe for humans, 402 for machines.

## Pricing your calls

A rule of thumb: `price = max(cost_of_compute * 2, 0.10 USDC)`. On Base a transfer costs <$0.01, so micro-pricing actually clears. The library also supports one-time unlocks if per-call is too granular.

## Beyond the middleware

The Pro tier ($19 one-time, license key) adds license issuance (Ed25519), a live on-chain watcher for payout monitoring, and a CLI to verify payments in CI — useful once you run more than one paid endpoint.

- Repo and docs: [usdc-paywall](https://github.com/josealbertomaquina/usdc-paywall)
- npm: `npm i @josealbertomaquina/usdc-paywall`

Questions on the verification model or the receipt TTL? Happy to go deeper in the comments.
